Certificates. Turnover. 9.1 Bidder Turn Over Criteria. The minimum average annual financial t urnover of the bidder during the last three years, ending on 31 st Mar of t he previous financial year should be as indicated in the bid document. Do cumentary evidence in the form of certified Audited Balance Sheets of Rel evant periods or a certificate from the Chartered Accountant/ Cost Accou ntant indicating the turnover details for the relevant period shall be uploa ded with the bid. The minimum average annual financial turn over of the OEM of the offered product during the last three years, ending on 31 st March of the previous financial year, should be as indicted in the bid document. Documentary evidence in the form of certified Audited Bal ance sheets of relevant period shall be uploaded with the bid. Payment shall be released only after submission of docu

mentary evidence of having functional service centre. 13. Past Project Experience. The bidder/OEM {themselves or through r eseller(s)}, should have executed project for supply and installation/ com missioning of same or similar category products during preceding 03 fina ncial years (i.e. current year and three previous financial year) as on open ing of bid, as per following criteria (i) Single order of at least 35% of estim ated bid value ; or (ii) Two orders of at least 20% each of estimated bid va lue : or (iii) Three orders of at least 15% each of estimated bid value. Satis factory performance certificates issued by respective buyer organization f or the above orders should be uploaded with bid. In case of bunch bid, the category related to primary product having highest bid value should meet this criterion. 14. Unlimited Liability clause/ certificate. The seller shall be liable for all losses, damages, claim and liabilities arising due to breach, negligence , default or failure at attributable to the seller in performance of the contr act, in accordance with the provisions of DPM 2025 and DAP 2020 as applicable. 15. Risk & Expense Clause. In case of foreign contracts, risk and expense cla use is generally not applicable, though there could be some exceptions. If, in ex ceptional circumstances, it is decided to include this clause in the RFP, procure ment provisions. y. 16.3 Bring up the issue of discrepancy in all meeting with the representati ve of supplier. 16.4 Provide for adequate performance bank guarantee to cover such risk s. 16.5 Approach the Government of the supplier’s country through the Ministry of Defence, if needed. 16.6 Consider de-registering the firm from the approved list of firms, if ne cessary. 17. Liquidated Damages. 17.1 Compensation of loss on account of last delivery where loss is pre-es timated and mutually agreed to is termed as the Liquidated Damage (LD), Law allows recovery of pre-estimated loss, provided such a term is included in the contract. For imposition of LD, there is no need to establis h actual loss due to late supply. The legal position with regard to claim for liquidated damages is as follows:- 17.1.1 Whatever the quantum of the loss sustained; the claim cannot exc eed the sum stipulated in the contact. 17.1.2 Only reasonable sum can be calculated as damages, which in give n situation may be less than the sum stipulated. 17.1.3 What is a reasonable sum would depend on facts. 17.1.4 Count may proceed on the assumption that the sum stipulated refl ects the genuine pre-estimates of the parties as t o the probable loss and such clause is intended to dispense with proof thereof. 17.1.5 The distinction between penalty and LD has been abolished by the Indian Contact Act and in every case, the court is not bound to award mor e than ‘reasonable compensation’ not exceeding the amount so named. 18. Termination of a concluded contract. A contract may be terminated in the fo ll owing circumstances:- 18.1 When the supplier fails to honour any parts of the contract including failure to deliver the contracted store/render services in time. 18.2 When the contractor is found to have made any false or fraudulent d eclaration or statement to get the contact or he is found to be indulging in unethical or unfair trade practices. 18.3 When both parties mutually agree to terminate the contract. 18.4 When the item offered by the supplier repeatedly fails in the inspecti on and/ or the supplier is not in a position to either rectify the defects or o ffer items conforming to the contract ed quality standards. 18.5 Any special circumstances, which must be recorded to justify the ca ncellation or termination of a contact. 19. The seller has no right to given, bar gain , sell, assign or sublet or otherwise dispose of thew contract or any pa rt t hereof, as well as to give or to let a third party take benefit or advantage of the present contract or any part thereof.

20. Fall Clause. In case where contracts have to be concluded with th e fi rms, whose rate contract with DGS&D/ Other central procurement agenci es has expired and renewal of RC has not taken place, a fall clause should be incorporated in the Supply order/ Contract to the effect that during the currency of the Supply order/ Contract, in ca se rates are found to be lowe r on conclusion of rate contract, the lower rates as in the rate contact shall be applicable. 21. Neither party shall bear responsibility for the comple te or partial non performance of any of its obligations (except for failure t o pay any sum which has become due on account of receipt of goods und er the provisions of the contract), if the no n performance results from suc h Force Majeure Circumstances as Flood, Fire, Earthquake and other acts of God, as well as War, Military Operations, blockade, Act s or Actions of St ate Authorities or any other circumstances beyond the control of the parti es that might arise after the conclusion of the contract. 22. Items delivered will be inspected by board of officers for fitness and acceptance. 23. Warranty Clause. 23.1 The warranty shall be valid for a period of 36 months from the date of final acceptance/ commissioning of the system at the consig nee unit, unless otherwise specified in the contract. 23.2 During the warranty period, any defect or malfunction notice d during normal use and attributable to design, material, workmans hi p or software/ firmware shall be rectified or replaced by the vendor at no additional cost, including cost of spares, labour, transportation and incidental expenses. 23.3 In case the defective equipment or components cannot be re p aired on site, the vendor shall arrange replacement with an equivalent or superior item within the stipulated time frame. 23.4 Timely servicing/ rectification of defects during warranty peri o d; After having been notified of the defects/ service requirement d u ring warranty period, Seller has to complete the requirement Servic e/ Rectification within 15 days time limit. If the seller fails to comple te service/ rectification with defined time limit, a penalty of 0.5% o f unit price of the product shall be charged as penalty for each we e k of delay from the seller, seller can deposit the penalty with the Buy er directly else the Buyer shall have a right to recover all such pen a lty amount from the performance Security (PBG). Cumulative Penalt y cannot exceed more than 10% of the total contract value after w hich the Buyer shall have the right to get the service/ rectification to the buyer. 24. Malicious Code Certificate. The vendor shall furnish a Malicious Co de Certificate in line with DAP-2020 requirements, certifying that the hard ware, filmware and software supplied are free from malicious logic, spywa re, backdoors or unauthorized embedded features. 25. DPIIT Registration. Submission of valid DPIIT registration/ certification, wh erever applicable, shall be mandatory in compliance with Government of India a nd DAP-2020 procurement policies. 26. Government Law and Jurisdiction. The contract shall be governed by the

construed in accordance shall be governed by and construed in accordance wit h the laws of India, and jurisdiction shall lie with courts a s decided by the purch aser in accordance with DAP-2020. 27. DIL License. The bidder/OEM shall possess a valid DIL License applicable to the offered equipment/system. Submission of a copy of the vali d DIL License al ong with the bid shall be mandatory. The license shall rem ain valid throughout the execution of the contract. 28. OEM Training. 28.1 The bidder/ OEM shall provide mandatory OEM level training for a pe riod of 15 days to the nominated personnel of the user unit. The trai ning shall cover operational, handling, maintenance, troubles hooting and other relevant aspects of the equipment. 28.2 Training Certificate. On successful completion of the training, the OE M shall issue a training completion certificate to the nominate d personnel . 28.3 Cost of Training. The complete cost of the 15 day OEM training inclu ding training material, instructor charges and other associated expenses shall be deemed included in the quoted price. No addition al payment shall be admissible on this account. 29. Shelf Life. A minimum shelf life of 06 years from the date of manufactur e. 30 Bid Terms/ Technical Specifications. The technical and functional s pecifications uploaded under "Buyer Added Bid Specific Additional Sco pe of Work" are specifically applicable to the procurement of 3800 x Su b Tactical Very Short Range Drones and shall form an integral part of t he Bid Document. The GeM Category specifications are generic in nature and the technical evaluation shall be carried out against the approved technical eval uation specified in the Bid Document "Buyer Added Bid Specific Additional Scope of Work", subject to applicable GeM provisions. .
